title: CFP Rankings overrated, underrated: Alabama's grip defies logic, Indiana deserves better - CBS Sports

body:
The same principle the CFP Selection Committee used to drop Indiana multiple spots a week ago clearly doesn't apply to Alabama
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:45 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Find someone who loves you as much as this College Football Playoff selection committee loves Alabama.The logic that seemed to apply to Indiana a week ago did not apply to Alabama this week. The Crimson Tide remained at No. 3 in the CFP Rankings despite all six SEC teams it has beaten this season losing over the weekend. A week ago, Indiana dropped five spots in a similar scenario. There's no doubt Alabama is a very good football team that is more than deserving of a playoff berth at this point. That's not in question. But if the committee is going to rank these teams 1 through 25 each week, we get to quibble over every single spot. And as it stands, it's hard to understand why Alabama is still ranked above Texas. The Longhorns have more top-25 wins (3 to 2) and rank above the Crimson Tide in strength of schedule, strength of record and game control. Alabama's best wins of the season are over No. 16 Kentucky and South Carolina, which is inexplicably still ranked No. 21 (more on that later). Texas has wins over No. 9 Tennessee (a team Alabama lost to), No. 14 Ohio State and No. 25 Ole Miss. It also knocked LSU out of the rankings with its win over the Tigers last Saturday. 
Alabama has Texas beat in terms of margin of victory, but should that truly be enough to trump all the other metrics?Evidently for the committee, it is. "I think when we look at Alabama and their consistency throughout the conference schedule," CFP chair Hunter Yurachek said Tuesday when I asked about what separated Alabama and Texas. "I mentioned their point spread in their conference games is close to 23 points a game; Texas is not in that same ballpark. I think just the consistency from one game to the next, even the consistency within a game. Texas had, after their win against LSU, five wins against teams ranked in our poll last week. That's changed a little bit with the poll this week, but Texas has got some really good wins."Texas is a really good football team, but the separator for us as a committee between the two is just the consistent play of Alabama throughout the season." 
Texas certainly fails the "eye test" at times. The Longhorns have the best resume but don't always look the best on the field. Even in Texas' win over LSU last weekend, it wasn't pretty. There's certainly an argument that Alabama has looked better than Texas at points this season. But focusing more on the eye test than a mountain of metrics is where the committee can get itself in trouble.No. 9 Tennessee also has an argument for being ranked above Alabama given its head-to-head win over the Crimson Tide. But it is clear the committee will continue to keep those two schools far enough apart in the rankings to justify not applying the head-to-head result, since they aren't in the same pod for direct comparison. That decision means the Volunteers have no margin for error this weekend if they lose to former coach Lane Kiffin's Tigers. You can only imagine the outrage there will be in Knoxville if that were to happen. Alabama is this week's most overrated team. 
        
            
                College Football Playoff bracket: What 12-team field would look like after third 2026 CFP rankings
                
                    Shehan Jeyarajah                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Underrated: TexasFor all the reasons listed above, the Longhorns should be the highest ranked-two loss team. If the committee is comfortable putting a two-loss Alabama team at the No. 3 spot ahead of undefeated UCLA, it should have done so for Texas. Ranked No. 5 in the country with two regular season weeks to go is nothing to sneeze at, but the Longhorns should be the two-loss SEC team in line for a bye right now. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Overrated: Ohio StateThe Buckeyes moved up six spots for…a nine-point win over an unranked Northwestern team. Yes, some of that is due to the attrition among teams ranked above Ohio State last week. But it's hard to make a viable argument that the Julian Sayin-less Ohio State team that lost to USC and Oregon and barely beat Northwestern is one of the 14 best teams in the country right now. There is terrific talent on the roster, including the all-world receiver Jeremiah Smith, but the Ohio State team I watched in person against Oregon looked broken and deflated. It's stunning, frankly, that that team may sneak into the playoff if a few more teams ranked above the Buckeyes lose in the next three weeks. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Underrated: IndianaCurt Cignetti, who used clown emojis to call out his team's ranking last week, may not have helped his cause with the selection committee. The Hoosiers moved up only one spot this week despite a 27-13 win over No. 18 USC. Indiana's weak non-conference scheduling is rightfully being taken into account, but the Hoosiers' lone loss of the season was to a full-strength Ohio State team. Indiana has a dominant defense that is capable of winning a championship. It felt like an overcorrection to drop Indiana from No. 4 to No. 9 a week ago. Unfortunately for the Hoosiers, there wasn't enough of a correction in their favor this week. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Overrated: South CarolinaThe Gamecocks at No. 21?! After losing to Arkansas 34-6?! I understand that not having LaNorris Sellers against the Razorbacks clearly had an impact. But there are some results that are so bad -- like losing 34-6 to Arkansas -- that it should drop you out of the rankings altogether. That a four-loss South Carolina team is still in the rankings gives ammunition to every critic out there who believes the committee continues to overrate the SEC. You could make similar arguments for Oklahoma, Florida and Ole Miss, which are also four-loss teams and also found a way to stay in the rankings. It has to be deeply frustrating not only for Big Ten teams like Illinois and Northwestern that no four-loss Big Ten team can get in, but also for the Group of Six squads like Liberty and Memphis who would be overjoyed to see themselves in the top 25.
Why does it matter? South Carolina staying in the top 25 gives Alabama another top 25 win which makes it easier for the committee to justify keeping the Tide in the top four. Similarly, Texas benefits from Ole Miss at No. 25 instead of Liberty or some other school.

        A lockout may be coming, but nobody told the hot stove. It's already burning bright with a series of mid-November signings.    Once the lockout becomes official, the signings -- and all other transactions -- will cease, but the ones that happen before then will still count toward whenever baseball is allowed to resume. So we'd better document them all here, just like any other offseason, breaking down their impact for Fantasy Baseball.    That's what Scott White and Chris Towers intend to do over the next few weeks, at least, before everything goes quiet. They'll eventually pick up where they left off when the hot stove heats up again in ... March? Hopefully not much later than that.    Whatever the timeline, you'll want this page bookmarked so you can get the first word on everything that happens.

He's a 32-year-old closer, and while he has mostly been a very good one over the past six seasons, there have been enough bumps in the road along the way to make the risk for Bednar pretty obvious. But from a Fantasy perspective, Bednar safely looks like a top-12 closer now that he's returning to the Yankees. His strikeout rate regressed in 2026, but his swinging-strike rate was actually higher than the previous season, and none of his underlying metrics otherwise really tell the story of a pitcher in decline. He's somewhere shy of the elite tier of closers for Fantasy, but he's good enough (and secure enough in his role for a good team) to be worth drafting as your primary source of saves. --Chris Towers Ryan Jeffers accepts Twins' qualifying offerIt was a mild surprise to see the Twins extend Jeffers the qualifying offer, but it's not a surprise to see him accept it. He came back from June 2025 Tommy John surgery to pitch effectively for the Dodgers in 2026, putting up a 3.46 ERA in 26 innings, and while the underlying data isn't quite as promising, he still missed a ton of bats and had good control. He's not necessarily a name you need to know for Draft Day in most leagues, but Phillips could be very relevant in 2027 if things go sideways for Suarez in the way they so often do for pitchers in their mid-30s. --Chris Towers

body:
Alberts is set to take over at Michigan, an athletic department plagued by recent scandals, with a football program underachieving under first-year coach Kyle Whittingham
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:33 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Texas A&M athletic director Trev Alberts has accepted the same position at Michigan, a source confirmed to CBS Sports. Alberts is leaving College Station after fewer than two years on the job. Alberts, a former All-American linebacker at Nebraska, was hired as athletic director at his alma mater in 2021. After only three years, he left to take the Texas A&M job, where he took over following the firing of Jimbo Fisher. Alberts did not hire Mike Elko, but worked closely with him as he reached the College Football Playoff in 2025. Now, he steps into the Michigan athletic director's chair, facing a pivotal moment in the school's history. The Wolverines are one year out from firing coach Sherrone Moore for cause after an inappropriate relationship with a subordinate and a subsequent arrest. His replacement, Kyle Whittingham, has been an unmitigated disaster, leading the Wolverines to a 5-5 record. Michigan already cut offensive coordinator Jason Beck, paying him a reported $7 million in buyout, believed to be the highest ever for an assistant coach. The Wolverines also benched former No. 1 quarterback Bryce Underwood, the highest-profile recruit in the modern era. Alberts will also oversee first-year basketball coach Mike Boynton, fresh off a national championship. 
Alberts signed a contract extension with Texas A&M last November through 2032. It was set to pay him more than $3 million per year. Hard decisionsAlberts arrived at Texas A&M in the wake of Jimbo Fisher's firing, which led to a $70+ million buyout, the largest in college football history. While the buyout was covered by private funds, Alberts made aggressive cuts to the athletic department budget to ensure financial solvency. He also helped lead negotiations for a 15-year, $515 million multimedia rights deal that included NIL considerations. At Michigan, his trials will be different. Michigan has been the most scandal-plagued athletic department in the past decade. Former coach Jim Harbaugh was at the center of two major NCAA scandals before he left for the Los Angeles Chargers, including the famous sign-stealing investigation centered on former staff member Connor Stalions. In addition to Moore, former Michigan offensive coordinator Matt Weiss was indicted for computer crimes in March 2025. 
Michigan desperately needs an adult in the room to help lead the athletic department towards consistency. At the same time, Alberts has his work cut out to match the level of success his predecessor, Warde Manuel, achieved. Frustration in College StationAlberts' departure from Texas A&M would come amidst a disappointing third season for coach Mike Elko. The Aggies are 4-6 and at serious risk of missing bowl eligibility for only the third time in the past 20 years. Elko signed a long-term extension with the program after reaching the College Football Playoff last season. 
Alberts is the third straight Texas A&M athletic director to leave for another job. Former AD Ross Bjork left to take the Ohio State job, while former AD Scott Woodward took over at LSU. The latter was later fired in Baton Rouge last year after the Brian Kelly hire failed.

title: Duke changes are necessary after Illinois routs home Blue Devils behind Andrej Stojakovic's historic game - CBS Sports
description: No. 5 Duke's issues are exposed in a record-breaking home loss to the No. 10 Fighting Illini
body:
No. 5 Duke's issues are exposed in a record-breaking home loss to the No. 10 Fighting Illini
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:39 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        If No. 5 Duke needed a recalibration after a wire-to-wire loss to Michigan State in the Champions Classic, it may need something far more drastic after Tuesday's debacle, a 99-78 shellacking at home at the hands of No. 10 Illinois. The Fighting Illini, short-handed and all, walked into Cameron Indoor Stadium and handed Jon Scheyer's club a loss that the Blue Devils won't soon forget. It's one of the most embarrassing beatdowns for Duke basketball in years, eliciting call-backs to 1989 to find the last time Duke lost by 20-plus points at home. Losing basketball games is part of the gig, and Duke has yielded more than its fair share of heartbreakers, but the way this one went down said a whole lot about the fabric of this Illinois team and equally as much about where Duke (3-2) is between the ears.     
        
            
                Trotter's Trends: A booming NIL market for 5-stars; Oregon State is the best offense you haven't heard about
                
                    Isaac Trotter                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Before their loss to the Illini, the Blue Devils had won 35 consecutive home games, the longest active streak in the country, including 22 consecutive victories vs. nonconference opponents.
   Stojakovic stuffs stat sheet in historic night     Illinois (4-1) is tough, resilient and owns one of the best duos in all of college basketball. Senior Andrej Stojakovic was en Fuego from the tip. The sleek wing drove Duke into its grave with devastating slashes to the cup. Stojakovic's 46-point explosion broke the record for the most points scored by a visitor in Cameron Indoor's hallowed halls set by South Carolina's Grady Wallace (43 points in 1957).       Rude visitors  The top scoring performances by a Duke opponent at Cameron Indoor Stadium.   	Player, Team		Date		Points		Andrej Stojakovic, Illinois		Nov. 17, 2026		46		Grady Wallace, South Carolina		Feb. 23, 1957		43		Len Bias, Maryland		Jan. 25, 1986		41		Frank Selvy, Furman		Dec. 2, 1953		40		Lennie Rosenbluth, North Carolina		March 1, 1957		40		Joe Smith, Maryland		March 1, 1995		40	It's tied for the second-most points an Illinois player has ever scored in a single game. But for some of the game, it was Illinois five-star freshman Quentin Coleman who somehow, someway looked like the best player on the floor. Coleman will make Duke regret not taking a stronger second look at recruiting the former Wake Forest commit. The slim 6-foot-4 guard made his best impression toward being the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NBA Draft with a 27-point, eight-rebound, four-assist showing. Illinois walloped Duke despite shooting just 19% from 3-point range because it had the best two players on the floor by a country mile.    It was an absolute splattering.    
    Duke off to rough start and it won't get any easier    Duke, for all intents and purposes, looks shattered right now. Physically, mentally, spiritually, all of the above. The Illini rebounded 18 of its 41 misses. An unacceptable, abominable mark for a Duke team that is the third-tallest in America. Jon Scheyer was so fed up with Duke's point guard play that he benched Cayden Boozer for all but three minutes in the second half. Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje, a potential No. 1 pick in 2028, was also riding the pine to start the second half.     
A starting lineup flip feels inevitable for Scheyer, but it's far more than just changing up personnel.     Two weeks ago, Duke had a starting lineup that was the envy of everyone. A point guard like Boozer who gets the ball where it needs to go. A sharpshooter like John Blackwell, who is equally as dangerous from beyond the stripe as he is with his boulder-shoulder drives. A big wing in Dame Sarr, who was on the short-list for National Defensive Player of the Year. A front line filled with Boumtje Boumtje (dubbed the No. 1 player in the sport this year by some outlets) and big man Pat Ngongba, who looked poised for an all-time year now that he's in the best shape of his life.    It wasn't hyperbole to dub Duke's starting lineup as the best in the country. It also couldn't be further from the truth on a night like this. Boozer, Blackwell, Sarr, Ngongba and Boumtje Boumtje are all blue-chip recruits who just got outplayed by an Illinois team that didn't have CBS Sports' Preseason All-American David Mirkovic sidelined with a broken foot. Duke got out-hustled by a team starting three freshmen. It's the first time since UNC in 2007 that a team with three diaper dandies in the starting lineup walked into Cameron and beat Duke. Coleman is the 5-star coup, but Ethan Brown and Lincoln Williams were three-star recruits. This isn't even the best version of Illinois. When Mirkovic gets cleared, that trio of Coleman, Stojakovic and Mirkovic is flat-out terrifying. Illinois looks like it has dudes. Duke has, what, exactly?
The best defenses take away — or limit —  what the opponent does best. Duke's defense? After you, please. Stojakovic gave Sarr, Sebastian Wilkins and anybody else the business. Illinois' coaching staff was jumping for joy when Duke senior guard Caleb Foster got switched onto Coleman. The freshman took the senior to school for an old-fashioned three-point play in the second half to keep the good orange-and-blue vibes rolling. Duke had nothing for Illinois at the point of attack or at the rim.Winning the NCAA Tournament? Duke can't even think about that right now. Not with a date with UConn lingering next week in Las Vegas. If Duke doesn't bring its hard hat to that Sin City showdown, UConn will pour salt into a fresh wound.    Burying a season is foolish in November, but Duke better stop digging because this hole is deep. Finding an ounce of toughness, more connectivity and an identity on both ends of the floor is paramount. Duke has nothing working right now on either end. No cutting. No offensive rebounding. No pace. It's a bunch of timid shots with soft drives and a shockingly low amount of physicality.     
You can't say that about Illinois. Time or score, healthy or not, you know what Illinois is going to do. The offensive rebounding, the unselfishness, the pace, the mismatch hunting. That's what the Illini do, day in and day out. Brad Underwood has made a living getting his team to be at its very best on the road in tough environments, even if they are short-handed. It happens year after year after year. Tuesday was Underwood's masterpiece, where all the buzzwords about culture, identity and slogans like "Everyday guys" start to garner more than just rolled eyes.    What can Duke hang its hat on right now? That it will rank highly in recruiting rankings?

body:
The Longhorns take over the top opening-round host spot after knocking off LSU, while Wake Forest snatches the bracket's final at-large bid
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:24 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        No. 5 Texas moved into a prime position after beating LSU over the weekend, setting itself up to be the highest-ranked first-round host in the College Football Playoff Rankings. The Longhorns jumped No. 6 Notre Dame, setting up a projected path of No. 12 Boise State and No. 4 UCLA to reach the national semis. At the back end, No. 11 Wake Forest jumped No. 12 Texas Tech to grasp Kentucky's vacant spot in the bracket, the final at-large in the field. They project to face Notre Dame in South Bend. No. 8 Indiana and No. 9 Tennessee also switched spots after the Hoosiers dominated USC to stay alive in the title race. Outside of those small moves, the rankings remained largely unchanged. The top four byes remain No. 1 Georgia, No. 2 Utah, No. 3 Georgia and No. 4 UCLA, giving both undefeated teams remaining passes through the first round. No. 12 Texas Tech, No. 13 Oregon and No. 14 Ohio State rank as the first three teams out of the field. Here is how the College Football Playoff bracket looks after the third CFP Rankings release of the 2026 season. 
                                                                    CBS Sports Grapg
                                                            Alabama remains strongLast week, Indiana's resume took a big hit when several of the best teams the Hoosiers faced suffered crushing losses. Despite the same happening to Alabama over the weekend with LSU, Mississippi State and Kentucky all falling, the Tide were totally insulated and remained at No. 3. 
Alabama has only one ranked win at this point, against No. 16 Kentucky. They have losses to both other ranked opponents, including a 26-10 loss to No. 9 Tennessee. It's baffling that the two teams rate so far apart. Closing bubbleWith two weeks of games left to go, along with conference championships, the top 12 of the playoff seems to be coming together. No. 11 and 12 are both 9-1 teams from the Big 12 and ACC, with No. 13 Oregon lurking at 7-3. Right now, Texas Tech is the first team out of the rankings at 9-1, despite beating then-No. 25 Oklahoma State over the weekend. Still, the Red Raiders are projected to reach the Big 12 Championship Game. Wake Forest will also have a second shot at Miami in a hypothetical ACC title game. 
Every team in the top 12 of the rankings can play their way in -- or out -- but it will likely come from that group.

The third College Football Playoff rankings are out, setting the stage for the final two weeks of the regular season

        The third edition of the College Football Playoff Rankings was released Tuesday night, and with the Week 11 results producing mostly chalk, there was very little movement at the top of this week's rankings. Georgia (9-1, 7-1 SEC) remains in the No. 1 spot on the heels of its emphatic win. The Bulldogs left no doubt they deserve to be recognized as the top team in the country after their beatdown of Missouri. With two regular-season games left against South Carolina and rival Georgia Tech, both of whom have failed to live up to expectations this season, the path is clear for Georgia to enter the SEC Championship Game with just one loss. With a win over the Gamecocks this weekend, the Dawgs will clinch their spot in Atlanta. Utah (10-0, 7-0 Big 12), meanwhile, holds steady in the No. 2 spot on Tuesday. The Utes kept their undefeated record intact in Week 11 with a thrilling win over Arizona on the road. Back-to-back wins over ranked teams have certainly impressed the College Football Playoff Selection Committee, and Utah remains on track for the program's first CFP appearance under first-year coach Morgan ScalleyAlabama, UCLA and Texas round out the top five in this week's CFP Rankings. While Notre Dame thrashed Boston College and remains firmly on track for a return to the CFP, Texas' thrilling win on the road at LSU was too hard to ignore for the committee. Thus, Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning and the Longhorns now sit among the top five as the season winds down. 
With the 12-team playoff model granting automatic bids to the five highest-ranked conference champions, Boise State would take the last spot if the field were chosen today from the Group of Six level, as the Broncos come in at No. 17.College Football Playoff Rankings, Nov. 17~ First-round byeGeorgia (9-1) ~Utah (10-0) ~Alabama (8-2) ~UCLA (10-0) ~Texas (8-2)Notre Dame (9-1)Miami (9-1)Indiana (9-1)Tennessee (8-2)BYU (8-2)Wake Forest (9-1)Texas Tech (9-1)Oregon (7-3)Ohio State (7-3)Iowa (8-2)Kentucky (7-3)Boise State (9-1)USC (7-3)Arizona (7-3)Houston (7-3)South Carolina (6-4)Oklahoma (6-4)Louisville (7-3)Florida (6-4)Ole Miss (6-4Analysis to come from CBS Sports Bowl expert Brad Crawford. Texas makes top-four caseWith a nation-leading seven victories over teams with winning records this season, including a pair currently ranked by the CFP, Steve Sarkisian's squad is peaking at an ideal time. Since being slotted at No. 7 in the initial rankings and moving up to No. 6 last week, the Longhorns are now fifth with a potentially favorable path to the semifinals if this holds. Arkansas and Texas A&M remain for Texas, then it's a potential three-team tiebreaker situation for second in the SEC for the right to play Georgia in the conference championship. The top-ranked Bulldogs solidify their right to defend their crown with a win at South Carolina on Saturday before awaiting their opponent. The Longhorns' two losses this season? Oklahoma and Florida, teams who are both ranked this week at 6-4 overall after wins over Ole Miss and Kentucky.
Alabama's resume hollows ... but committee doesn't care The Crimson Tide did not move off their No. 3 ranking despite Week 11's results within the SEC butchered Alabama's season-long resume. While the CFP Selection Committee's strength of record metric is private, Kentucky's loss to Florida, South Carolina's stunner at Arkansas and LSU losing in the final seconds to Texas weakened the Crimson Tide's three best wins this fall. The Wildcats dropped out of the top 12, the Gamecocks slipped from No. 17 to No. 21 and Lane Kiffin's Tigers are no longer ranked.The selection committee did not show any consistency this week with Alabama's ranking following the win at Vanderbilt. In last week's rankings, CFP chair Hunter Yurachek attributed Indiana's five-spot drop — despite that team being off — to six of the Hoosiers' Power Four opponents losing. Over the weekend, six of Alabama's Power Four opponents suffered the same fate. Did it matter? Not a bit."Three things happened to Indiana last week — one was the conference losses, two were five games involving top-14 teams, and three, Indiana had a bye," Yurachek said Tuesday night. "This week Alabama faced similar circumstances, but it didn't have the same impact on Alabama's strength of schedule than it had on Indiana."
One of three SEC teams with matching 8-2 records, which includes a pair of conference losses, Alabama's clearest path back into the top four is handling its business against Chattanooga and Auburn before potentially squaring off with Georgia in the SEC Championship Game. The winner of next month's finale in Atlanta will assuredly get a first-round bye, but it's no guarantee the Crimson Tide get there and a second crack at Georgia. Alabama does not control its destiny in the SEC title game race since it lost to Tennessee head-to-head and, in the event of a two-way tie in the second with Texas, would not advance since the Longhorns would have a 4-0 record against common opponents.Who's on the actual bubble?Looking at Nos. 10-15 this week, there's been fluctuation from the committee. Kentucky's on the outside looking in following its second consecutive SEC loss, while impressive road wins by Texas Tech and Wake Forest have moved the Red Raiders and Demon Deacons to Nos. 12 and 11, respectively. No. 15 Iowa and No. 13 Oregon — along with 14th-ranked Ohio State — are still mathematically alive in the Big Ten championship discussion, but chaos is needed. The likelihood of the Big Ten being a three-bid league is slim unless at-large hopefuls in front of the Ducks, Buckeyes and Hawkeyes drop a game between now and Selection Sunday.The biggest move was Ohio State moving up six spots to No. 14, including one spot ahead of Iowa. The Buckeyes have a head-to-head win over the Hawkeyes despite a worse record and therefore have been slotted ahead of Iowa.
Second-ranked Utah, No. 10 BYU and Texas Tech are all single-digit favorites on the road this weekend in the Big 12, while Wake Forest should cruise to its eighth straight win over Georgia Tech. Texas Tech and Wake Forest are the only bubble teams in control of their destiny by winning out and seizing auto-bids as conference champions.No team within the Power Four has looked as dominant as the Demon Deacons over the last four weeks. They've outscored three ACC opponents and Merrimack 145-0 in the first half during that stretch and could earn a quality win for victory No. 11 in the finale over Duke on Nov. 28.Wake Forest appears to be in great shape for one of two remaining at-large spots, with BYU or Texas Tech being our guess to grab the other. As for the other 10 teams we consider to be firmly in the field, they would have to play themselves out by struggling over the final two games to not appear in the bracket.

body:
Arsenal test their momentum against high-flying Lyonnes while Chelsea look to stay perfect defensively against PSG as the race for quarterfinal byes heats up

        There is no more room for error in the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League. After four matchdays, the league phase has been whittled down to only two games left for each of the 18 clubs, and the margin between a bye into the quarterfinals and an extra round of knockout playoffs in February will come down to dwindling points.OL Lyonnes rule the league phase at the moment. They top the tournament table with ten points, level with FC Barcelona but with a superior goal difference. Just behind the two Champions League contenders are Bayern Munich and Arsenal, with Chelsea FC and Manchester City creeping closer to the top four. Out of the 18 clubs competing, only four will earn direct berths to the quarterfinals, and eight will compete for a future spot alongside them. The final six clubs with the least amount of points will see their Champions League dream end, so matchday 5 will be a crucial turning point for several teams.Fighting for top spot positioning will be Arsenal and OL Lyonnes, and Chelsea against Paris Saint-Germain. HB Koge, Roma, and tournament debutants Inter Milan are level on four points and need to be in full urgency mode if they're to leapfrog and remain in contention for future rounds.
Here's what to watch on Matchday 5:UWCL ScheduleWednesday, Nov. 18BK Hacken vs. Manchester City, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)Real Madrid vs. Inter, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)   Chelsea vs. Paris Saint-Germain, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)   Juventus vs. OH Leuven, 3 p.m. (Paramount+) Thursday, Nov. 19 Austria Wien vs. Bayern Munich, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)   Paris FC vs. HB Koge, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)  Arsenal vs. OL Lyonnes, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)   Barcelona vs. Servette, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)  Benfica vs. Roma, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)Arsenal vs. OL LyonnesFans could get a glimpse of a future round when Arsenal take on OL Lyonnes on Thursday. The Gunners now have the tall task of tackling the French giants after battling Barcelona to a 1-1 draw at Camp Nou last week.A strong team defensive performance, anchored by goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez against the current title holders, and the inclusion of Frida Maanum in the attack were key difference-makers. Manager Renee Slegers and her side seem to be turning the page, with better results after questionable tactics and player availability raised concerns about the club's earlier performances. 
Taking on OL Lyonnes also won't be easy. The top French side has scored 20 goals through four league phase matches, and Marie-Antoinette Katoto leads the competition's Golden Boot race with seven goals. U.S. women's national team defensive midfielder Lily Yohannes is getting more lethal in the tournament and scored in her second consecutive tournament match during OL's 6-0 blowout against Juventus.
The eight-time Champions League winners will go up against an English club with plenty of momentum following last week's results against Barcelona. The Gunners have more players available to shake things up on the pitch, and Alessia Russo remains a threat after her hat trick against Benfica and has four goals in the league phase.Chelsea vs. Paris Saint-GermainChelsea FC will host PSG and the Blues are riding high on stout defensive performances. They co-lead the tournament alongside OL Lyonnes with zero goals conceded through four league phase games. 
The London side will need to be far better in attack if they want to claim being a top contender, though it's not for lack of trying. They're coming off a scoreless draw against BK Hacken, where they recorded a whopping 32 shots but only six attempts on target. U.S. women's national team winger Alyssa Thompson is still a factor with her swift technique and could help stretch PSG's backline, while Wieke Kaptein gets into dangerous spaces. Kaptein created both goals in Chelsea's 2-0 win against Roma, and the Dutch player has one goal and two assists in the tournament.PSG's fortunes seem to be turning for the worse after a promising start to the competition. They're in 10th place on the table now with five points and just one win in their last four games. The loss of Sakina Karchaoui with an ankle injury for the remainder of the league phase is a blow to the roster, though Naomie Feller, with two goals and two assists, is a threat for the Parisians.Desperation mode activatedThere are plenty of teams on the lower side of the table and running out of time. Alongside PSG with necessary urgency are Juventus, who were just beaten by OL Lyonnes, 6-0, and face a desperate 17th-place OH Leuven before closing out the league phase against PSG. It makes the penultimate meeting with OH Leuven almost a must win for Juventus, to lessen the stress on the final matchday.
A particularly intriguing matchup between ninth-place Benfica and 12th-place Roma could shake up the league table with a win by either side. If Roma's Kayleigh van Dooren and Alayah Pilgrim stay active on offense again, it could be a tough challenge for Benfica.

title: Christian Pulisic bicycle kick sparks USMNT to 2-0 rout of Haiti in Mauricio Pochettino farewell - CBS Sports
description: Julian Hall also scored while the Americans capped an 8-0 aggregate win before their manager departs for Manchest
body:
Julian Hall also scored while the Americans capped an 8-0 aggregate win before their manager departs for Manchester United

        In a farewell for Mauricio Pochettino before he heads to Manchester United, the United States men's national team were able to defeat Haiti 2-0 on Tuesday night, advancing in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals 8-0 on aggregate. Christian Pulisic opened the scoring with a bicycle-kick goal to kick things off, which was the emphatic send-off that was needed prior to Pochettino arriving in Manchester, but the USMNT were able to keep things up in the celebration in Cincinnati.
Julian Hall followed with a poacher's goal as Weston McKennie played orchestrator, and it continued a theme that whoever ends up taking over the national team will have tough decisions ahead. Folarin Balogun is struggling for minutes with Monaco and is looking to make a move at the end of the season, and Hall has done everything that he can to increase his own standing with five goals in six games for the USMNT.The New York Red Bulls star has a ways to go considering that he's still only 18 and will need to gain experience against top teams in the world instead of just Haiti, but he also can't ask for a better start than what he has gotten off to. It's why this is such an attractive job for whoever takes over the USMNT. They'll be able to build upon the good that Pochettino has instilled; the talent is there to move the squad forward, and there's plenty to love about the youth of the USMNT.
And alongside that, Pulisic has essentially screamed don't forget about me. During this camp, the Milan man has followed up on signing a new contract with the club by reaching 35 national team goals, moving into fourth all time for the USMNT over Eric Wynalda. Diego Kochen added to the good vibes with a third straight clean sheet, and Neil Pierre was even able to be cap-tied against the nation that he's also eligible for as the full-circle moments were left and right.Pulisic, the former 17-year-old phenom, was subbed off for Cavan Sullivan, the current 17-year-old phenom, and while the goal difference may have been larger in the first leg between these sides, this felt like a more measured performance despite the strangeness of Pochettino's assistants heading to United while he managed the squad prior to catching his own charter.
This camp had every chance of being a disaster given the circumstances of Pochettino leaving, but all parties did what was needed during this camp. All dual nationals were capped, including Santiago Castaneda, showing that even on his way out, Pochettino made sure to take care of the future of the federation. On to the next round of the Concacaf Nations League with a new manager and no complaints with the performance so far for the squad.

247Sports director of scouting Adam Finkelstein, who watched Lukic up close earlier this month, describes the 17-year-old standout as a jumbo wing "with an overlap of perimeter size and well-rounded ball-skills" and crafty passer.
"He's a good ball-handler and passer who moves without the ball and can even initiate some possessions," Finkelstein writes in his advanced scouting report. Fulwiley, who has been released on bond, is facing five charges, including flight from an officer, aggravated assault and aggravated battery

        LSU women's basketball star MiLaysia Fulwiley was arrested in Baton Rouge on Saturday after allegedly striking a police officer with a vehicle before fleeing the scene. Fulwiley is facing five charges, including flight from an officer, aggravated assault and aggravated battery. Fulwiley has been released on bond, but was not with LSU during their 116-70 win over Troy on Monday. LSU coach Kim Mulkey did not address the matter. "I truly think we gave a statement," Mulkey said after the game. "The university did, and that's all I'm willing to say right now until I gather more information."LSU told CBS Sports in a statement on Sunday that they "are aware of the situation and have no further comment at this time as it's an ongoing legal matter."Fulwiley posted a since-deleted statement to what appears to be her social media account on Sunday afternoon accusing the officers of lying:
"i would NEVER in my life hit a police ! WHY would i hit a police and run knowing who i am and what i do ! PLEASE DONT BELIEVE EVERYTHING YOU SEE !," Fulwiley wrote. Fulwiley was allegedly weaving through traffic on Saturday night when an officer directing traffic ordered her to stop, according to WBRZ. After coming to a stop and handing her license to the officer, Fulwiley was asked to reverse, according to police records. She allegedly put the car in reverse, then drove forward and struck an officer with the right side of the vehicle before fleeing the scene. Later, another officer cut off Fulwiley's car, and both Fulwiley and her passenger were removed from the vehicle and placed into custody, according to police.
East Baton Rouge District Attorney Hillar Moore said Monday that he was still awaiting reports on the incident. Louisiana State Police also issued a statement on Monday, which read, in part:"As with all arrests, the circumstances will be reviewed by the District Attorney's office. DPS personnel are compiling all available dash-camera, body-worn camera, and surrounding video footage, along with a comprehensive, documented report, for submission to the 19th Judicial District Attorney's Office for review. In accordance with established procedures, camera footage related to ongoing investigations is not routinely released to the media."Fulwiley transferred to LSU in 2025 after spending her first two collegiate seasons at South Carolina. She is the reigning back-to-back SEC Sixth Player of the Year and is currently projected as a top 10 pick in the 2027 WNBA Draft. 
Through her first four games this season, Fulwiley is averaging 17.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 4.3 assists, 4.3 steals and 2.8 blocks on 54.9% shooting. LSU is off to a 4-0 start and is ranked No. 9 in the country. The Tigers will be in action next on Monday against Troy.

title: Yankees' David Bednar, Twins' Ryan Jeffers accept qualifying offer, six others reject $23.15 million QO - CBS Sports
description: Jake Bauers has already agreed to a four-year deal with the Red Sox; now the other five will look for better offe
body:
Jake Bauers has already agreed to a four-year deal with the Red Sox; now the other five will look for better offers than the QO
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Two players have accepted this year's one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET. deadline, and six others have declined the QO. David Bednar (Yankees) and Ryan Jeffers (Twins) are returning to their teams, for the 2027 season, while Randy Arozarena (Mariners),  Brandon Lowe (Pirates), Adrian Morejon (Padres), Trevor Rogers (Orioles), and Seiya Suzuki (Cubs) are all hitting the market.An eighth free agent, Jake Bauers, also received the QO. He agreed to a four-year, $58 million contract with the Red Sox this past weekend. Effectively, Bauers declined the QO. Because they paid CBT in 2026, the Red Sox will surrender their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign Bauers. The Brewers, as a revenue-sharing receiver, will receive a compensation draft pick after the first round because the contract exceeds $50 million.The five unsigned free agents who rejected the QO are now tied to draft pick compensation. Their former teams will receive a draft pick if they sign elsewhere, and their new teams will be docked a draft pick and potentially international bonus pool money to sign them. The exact compensation depends on the team's revenue sharing and competitive balance tax (CBT) status.Here is draft pick compensation the former teams will receive if the seven qualified free agents change teams:
Free agentFormer teamCompensation draft pickRandy ArozarenaMarinersPick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50MBrandon LowePiratesPick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M  Adrian MorejonPadresPick after fourth roundTrevor RogersOriolesPick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M  Seiya SuzukiCubsPick after fourth roundCBT payors, like the Red Sox, will forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign a qualified free agent. Teams that receive revenue sharing will surrender their third-highest 2027 draft pick. All other teams will surrender their second-highest 2027 draft pick and $500,000 in 2027 international bonus pool money.It must be noted that declining the QO does not mean the free agent can not return to his former team. The two sides could still work out a contract of any size and any length, including one worth less than QO, though that is very unlikely. Zac Gallen, Michael King, and Kyle Schwarber rejected the QO last offseason and then later re-signed with their teams. Free agents must meet certain criteria to be eligible for the QO. Players cannot have received the QO previously and they must have spent the most recent season with one team, meaning anyone traded in-season is ineligible. The Dodgers could not give Tarik Skubal, far and away the offseason's best free agent, the QO following his midseason acquisition.The QO is set at the average of the top 125 salaries in the most recent season and that is salaries only, not total compensation. For example, the Yankees paid Cody Bellinger a $20 million signing bonus and a $32.5 million salary in 2026. Only the $32.5 million counts toward the QO calculation. This QO was worth a record $23.15 million this winter.The current QO system replaced the old free-agent arbitration system in 2012 and will remain in effect this offseason. The upcoming collective bargaining agreement could change the QO system, if not eliminate it entirely. Entering the offseason, just 18 of the 157 free agents to receive the QO accepted it. That count is now at 20 of 165.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    David BednarOne of the more effective closers in baseball last season, Bednar closed down 35 of 39 save chances with a 2.47 ERA, 1.04 WHIP and 76 strikeouts in 69 ⅓ innings. Having him back on board means the Yankees don't need to find a new closer and can look instead to shore up the bridge to the ninth as needed.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Ryan JeffersThere had been talk that Jeffers wanted to stay with the Twins but that he'd decline the QO and then negotiate a long-term deal. There's still room to reach an extension, of course, but he now doesn't have any leverage from outside offers. It's a big win for the Twins, with Jeffers resuming his role as the everyday catcher and Victor Caratini serving as the primary backup. Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 (127 OPS+) with 14 homers and 56 RBI is only 92 games last season. He's been one of the most productive offensive catchers in baseball over the course of the last four seasons, when healthy.

title: How Sky GM Jeff Pagliocca set up WNBA rivals for success and left Chicago reeling - CBS Sports
description: The Chicago Sky were the only team watching the 2027 WNBA Draft Lottery on Sunday that was hoping for bad luck. The Sky went 16-28 last
body:
The Chicago Sky were the only team watching the 2027 WNBA Draft Lottery on Sunday that was hoping for bad luck. The Sky went 16-28 last season and haven't made the playoffs since 2023, but owe the Washington Mystics a 2027 first-round pick swap to complete a 2025 trade. The Mystics made the playoffs last season, so the pick was gone no matter what, but the higher it landed in the lottery, the worse the trade would look for the Sky. In the end, it came up at No. 3, right where it was projected based on the odds. Washington, which already has one of the brightest futures in the league, is now guaranteed to add one of JuJu Watkins, Hannah Hidalgo or Madison Booker. Chicago, which has one of the bleakest futures, will get Washington's No. 11 pick. So it has gone for the Sky since general manager Jeff Pagliocca's arrival. Since he was hired on Halloween in 2023, he has wheeled and dealed to little success for Chicago, while simultaneously setting up three other teams -- the Atlanta Dream, Washington Mystics and Minnesota Lynx -- with young franchise players. Angel Reese, Sonia Citron and Olivia Miles have all either been drafted by the Sky or with picks the Sky originally owned since Pagliocca took charge; none of them play in Chicago. Now, it looks like the Mystics will add one of Hidalgo or Booker, and that's not even the end of the misery, because Washington also owns the Sky's 2028 first-round pick outright. 
Here's a list of notable players and picks that have been traded away during Pagliocca's three-year tenure:Kahleah CopperJulie AllemandRebekah GardnerMarina MabreyDana EvansSonia Citron (No. 3 pick in 2025)Angel ReeseAriel AtkinsOlivia Miles (No. 2 pick in 2026)Frieda Bühner (No. 17 pick in 2026)No. 3 pick in 20272028 first-round pickOf course, some of these players asked out due to issues that pre-dated Pagliocca, but an absurd amount of talent has left Chicago (or never arrived) over the last three years.Following Sunday's draft lottery, let's take a look back at Pagliocca's first three years in Chicago to see how things have gone so wrong for the Sky, but so right for the teams that have traded with them.2024Trades Kahleah Copper to PhoenixPagliocca's first big move was trading 2021 Finals MVP Kahleah Copper and the rights to Morgan Bertsch to the Mercury for Brianna Turner, Michaela Onyenwere, the No. 3 pick in the 2024 WNBA Draft, Phoenix's 2026 first-round pick and some second-round picks. Copper would go on to help the Mercury reach the Finals in 2025. However, Copper wanted to leave Chicago and Pagliocca got a great return. This deal was a positive start to his tenure. 
Trades Julie Allemand to Los AngelesA few weeks after moving Copper, Pagliocca traded veteran point guard Julie Allemand to the Sparks for the No. 8 pick in the 2024 draft and the rights to Li Yueru. Allemand had only played two seasons in the WNBA to that point, had sat out in 2023 and ended up sitting out in 2024 as well. Again, another nice deal to acquire a top-10 pick. Trades Rebekah Gardner to New YorkA month later, Pagliocca traded Rebekah Gardner to the New York Liberty in exchange for two second-round picks. Gardner had missed most of the 2023 season with a broken foot and has never been the same player she was pre-injury. Another solid move. Trades for No. 7 pickJust before the 2024 WNBA Draft, Pagliocca acquired the No. 7 pick and Sika Koné from the Minnesota Lynx in exchange for the No. 8 pick, the rights to Nikolina Milić, a 2026 first-round pick swap and a second-round pick. This is where the wheels started to fall off. Giving up a future first-round swap at the beginning of a rebuild was unnecessarily risky and would come back to haunt them. 
Drafts Kamilla Cardoso and Angel ReeseIn the 2024 WNBA Draft, Pagliocca selected Kamilla Cardoso (No. 3) and Angel Reese (No. 7). Immediately, there were major questions about drafting two bigs who could not space the floor just as the league was moving toward a more perimeter-oriented game. The Sky's interest in Reese was an open secret ahead of the draft, which made their decision to draft Cardoso at No. 3 even more confusing. In a vacuum, Cardoso was a very reasonable pick at No. 3, but if they were confident in getting Reese at No. 7, why not draft Rickea Jackson -- the best wing in the class -- at No. 3? (Ironically, Jackson is now on the team.)Pagliocca's belief in Reese was well-founded, and she became the steal of that draft. Cardoso, on the other hand, has never developed the way anyone hoped. While she's put up solid numbers throughout her career, she has not impacted winning. Let's take a look at the on/off data from Cardoso and Reese's two seasons together in Chicago. 
LineupMinutesNet RatingCardoso and Reese1,168-5.1Reese only884-3.7Cardoso only803-19.4Trades Marina Mabrey to ConnecticutAhead of the 2024 trade deadline, Pagliocca tarded Marina Mabrey and a second-round pick to the Connecticut Sun in exchange for Rachel Banham, Moriah Jefferson, the Sun's 2025 first-round pick and a 2026 first-round pick swap. Mabrey requested a trade, and getting a first-round pick and a pick swap for someone who, to that point, had never made an All-Star appearance, was a nice bit of business, especially given the lack of leverage. 2025Trades with Connecticut for Rebecca Allen Pagliocca's first move of the 2025 offseason was to trade Lindsay Allen and Milić to the Sun for Rebecca Allen. This was a smart deal that just didn't pan out. Lindsay Allen and Milić have done nothing since then, and it wasn't Pagliocca's fault that Rebecca Allen had one of the worst 3-point shooting seasons of her career in 2025. Trades Dana Evans to Las VegasDana Evans, who was part of the 2021 championship team, was a restricted free agent in 2025 and made it clear she wanted a bigger role. In a sign-and-trade deal, Pagliocca traded Evans to the Aces for two second-round picks in the 2025 draft, which later became Maddy Westbeld and Aicha Coulibaly. Westbeld is no longer with the Sky, but Coulibaly had some promising moments as a rookie in 2026. Getting two swings in the draft for a player who wanted to leave in free agency was decent business. Trades No. 3 pick to WashingtonThe Sky went 13-27 in 2024 and received the No. 3 overall pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft, which put them in a tricky spot. At the time, Paige Bueckers and Olivia Miles (who ended up staying in school) were expected to go 1-2 in that draft, which meant the Sky were going to have to reach to get the guard they really needed at No. 3, take a big, even though they had just drafted Cardoso and Reese, or trade the pick. Pagliocca chose the latter and decided to make a win-now move. In late February, he sent the No. 3 pick, a 2027 first-round pick swap and a 2027 second-round pick to the Mystics in exchange for Ariel Atkins. Atkins was a two-time All-Star and five-time All-Defensive honoree who had won a title with the Mystics in 2019 and gold medals with Team USA at the 2020 Olympics and 2022 World Cup. While everyone expected that Atkins would make the Sky better, the deal was widely criticized at the time as a short-sighted overpay -- especially when the Sky were so far away from making any serious noise in the playoffs and Atkins was set to be an unrestricted free agent in 2026. The Mystics ended up taking Sonia Citron at No. 3, who exceeded all expectations and is now one of the best young players in the league. She's been an All-Star in each of her first two seasons, won a gold medal with Team USA at the 2026 World Cup and was named to the All-Defensive Team last season. Atkins was solid in what wound up being her lone season in Chicago: 13.1 points, 3.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.6 steals, but she did not move the needle. In fact, the Sky were actually worse in 2025 than they were in 2024. They finished in a tie for last place at 10-34, which at the time set the single-season losses record. Giving up Citron for one season of Atkins would have been a disaster on its own, but now it's Citron and the No. 3 pick in the 2027 draft. Just a total disaster. This will go down as one of the worst deals in WNBA history. Trades for No. 11 pickJust before the 2025 WNBA Draft, Pagliocca swung a deal with the Lynx to acquire the No. 11 pick in exchange for extinguishing the 2026 first-round pick swap between the two teams. As a result, the Lynx got the Sky's 2026 first-round pick outright. 
The Lynx were coming off a Finals appearance and were one of the favorites heading into the 2025 season, while the Sky were coming off a 10-win campaign. The pick swap was almost certainly going to convey in 2026 (and it did), so Pagliocca took the No. 11 pick in 2025 rather than what would have been the No. 15 pick in 2026. Decent value bet that ultimately didn't work out. Drafts Ajša Sivka and Hailey Van LithThe Sky had the Nos. 10 and 11 picks in the 2025 WNBA Draft via Connecticut and Minnesota. At No. 10, Pagliocca selected Ajša Sivka and at No. 11 he took Hailey Van Lith. Sivka stayed in Europe in 2025 and eventually chose to go the college route. She is now a freshman at Kentucky, where she's off to a stellar start. The Sky retain her rights, and this may wind up being a great pick in the long run. Van Lith barely played during her rookie season and was waived during training camp in 2026. 
Giving up Citron, then getting nothing (at least so far) from your other two first-round picks in that class was a major setback for the Sky. The Van Lith pick, in particular, was a major error, especially after trading with the Lynx to cancel the 2026 swap rights and take the No. 11 pick. 2026Buys protection from the double expansion draftAhead of the 2026 season, the league held a double expansion draft for the Portland Fire and Toronto Tempo. The current teams were allowed to protect five players from selection. Pagliocca opted to ensure that neither the Fire nor the Tempo selected any Sky players by buying protection. 
He traded the No. 17 overall pick to the Fire for the No. 21 overall pick and a promise not to select any Sky players. He also traded the No. 26 overall pick to the Tempo for a promise not to select any Sky players. The Fire selected Frieda Bühner at No. 17, who had a promising rookie season. The Sky took Latasha Lattimore at No. 21; she did not make their roster. The Tempo took Shaffron Shiels at No. 26; she remained overseas last season. Were these deals the end of the world? No, but they were further examples of poor asset management. The 2025 Sky didn't have more than five players worth protecting, and dropping out of the top-20 and giving up another second-round pick in the process cost them a chance at Bühner, Charlisse Leger-Walker and Cassandre Prosper, all of whom were contributing players as rookies last season. Trades Angel Reese to AtlantaThe relationship between Reese and the Sky deteriorated quickly toward the end of the 2025 season. Reese gave a controversial interview to the Chicago Tribune in which she criticized the front office, coaching staff and her teammates, and insinuated that she would not re-sign after her rookie contract was up if the team's fortunes didn't change. 
Reese later apologized to her teammates and the organization, both publicly and privately, and the team suspended her for the first half of a game against the Aces -- a strange decision that only inflamed the situation. While Reese said in Dec. 2025 that she planned to return to the Sky, a split always seemed possible. Sure enough, Pagliocca traded her to the Atlanta Dream for first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 as soon as the league was open for business last offseason. While ESPN reported that Reese did not demand a trade, she did work with the organization on trade talks to find her a new team. The trade was immediately regarded as a disaster for the Sky that only got worse as the season went along. Reese won Defensive Player of the Year, made the All-WNBA Second Team and All-Defensive First Team, and led the Dream to the Finals, while the Sky went 16-28 and missed the playoffs again. Meanwhile, the Sky had to give up the No. 2 overall pick in the draft to the Lynx, which closed the book on the trade that brought Reese to Chicago in the first place. The Lynx drafted Miles, who was named the unanimous Rookie of the Year. Trades 2028 first to Washington
Amid a frenzy of moves last offseason, Pagliocca traded the Sky's 2028 first-round pick to the Mystics for Jacy Sheldon. While it was one thing to have interest in the former No. 5 overall pick as a reclamation project, giving up a 2028 first-round pick for her was baffling in the moment and could get exponentially worse. Sheldon averaged 6.4 points and 1.8 assists, and shot a career-worst 30% from 3-point range as the Sky finished 10 games out of the playoffs. Her poor play was part of the reason the Sky wound up in the lottery again and had to give the Mystics the No. 3 pick. Which, in turn, will make it more likely that the Sky miss the playoffs again next season and have to give the Mystics another lottery pick in 2028. Pagliocca can argue that he was put in a bad spot or had some bad luck on some of his previous trades. Not so on this one. This trade never made sense, and could result in the Sky giving up lottery picks in four consecutive drafts. It's particularly confusing how Pagliocca was swindled by the Mystics again before the 2025 deal was even complete. Trades Atkins to Los AngelesSpeaking of the 2025 deal with the Mystics, Pagliocca's third trade last offseason was flipping Atkins to the Sparks for Rickea Jackson -- the No. 4 pick in the 2024 draft, whom he should have selected at the time at No. 3 instead of Cardoso. Pagliocca rightfully received praise for finding a way to flip Atkins for a young player with All-Star potential and salvaging some value from the 2025 Mystics trade. Jackson was excellent to start last season, and helped the Sky get off to a 3-1 start before tearing her ACL. She missed the remainder of 2026, and it's unclear when she'll be available in 2027. Jackson's injury was a short- and long-term disaster. Her absence played a big role in the Sky missing the playoffs, which meant giving up the No. 3 pick. And it's unclear when she'll be back on the court again, or if she'll get back to her pre-injury level. If she's not available and at her best for most of the 2027 season, there's a good chance the Sky have to give up another lottery pick to the Mystics in 2028. Drafts Gabriela Jaquez ahead of Kiki RiceWhile the Sky had to give up the No. 2 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft to the Lynx, they did still have a lottery selection via the Sun, which checked in at No. 5. In a major shock, Pagliocca selected Gabriela Jaquez ahead of former UCLA teammate Kiki Rice and Flau'jae Johnson. Rice was always a much better pro prospect than Jaquez, and the Sky needed a point guard for the future. While Jaquez got off to a great start as a rookie, she soon faded and was out of the rotation for a stretch late in the season. There's still a good chance she's a solid player, but Rice, who made the All-Rookie Team despite playing just 28 games due to a severe ankle sprain, looks like a future All-Star. What's next?Turnarounds are always possible in the WNBA, but the future is murky for the Sky.The collection of players that have been traded away from the Sky in the past three years have combined for seven All-Star appearances, two All-WNBA appearances, two All-Defensive appearances, one Defensive Player of the Year and one Rookie of the Year award, three Finals appearances and one championship since leaving Chicago. Those accolades are going to keep rising because Reese, Miles and Citron, in particular, are three of the best young players in the league. And if the No. 3 pick in 2027 and the 2028 first-round pick are even close to that trio's level, the Sky's misery will only get worse.

title: Josh Hokit calls for rematch with Ciryl Gane after disputed loss at UFC 334 - CBS Sports

Gane poked Hokit in the eye early in round 1 of their heavyweight championship fight

        Josh Hokit came up just short of capturing the UFC heavyweight championship with a spirited effort against champion Ciryl Gane at UFC 334 this past Saturday. Now, Hokit is calling for a rematch with Gane and using an early Gane eye poke as a primary reason for another shot at gold.Early in the first round of their fight at Madison Square Garden in New York, Gane reached toward Hokit's face and his finger clearly went into Hokit's eye. Hokit reacted to the foul, but referee Marc Goddard did not see it, and thus, Gane was not punished.Hokit would go on to lose a narrow unanimous decision that many felt he had edged out through the application of relentless pressure that forced Gane out of his comfort zone as a tactical striker. Still, the judges favored Gane's striking edge over Hokit's pressure, and Hokit was not able to capture heavyweight gold just over one year after making his Octagon debut.On Tuesday, Hokit responded to a video of former middleweight champion Robert Whittaker breaking down the fight by calling for an immediate rematch, addressing his Tweets to UFC and promotion CEO Dana White.

Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!"He completely poked my eye out 40 [seconds] into the fight," Hokit wrote. "I complained and got no help. Blinded, I had every excuse to walk away and blow up the entire event. But I didn't quit on you, and I didn't quit on the fans. I care about this sport way too much to ever take the easy way out. I'm not a bitch. Most people know I won that night. Thats why I am making the case that we should run it back."Hokit also cited how he believes the scoring criteria of the Unified Rules of Mixed Martial Arts should have resulted in the decision going in his favor.

        
            
                UFC 334 fight fallout: Best options for Ciryl Gane, Josh Hokit, Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes after Saturday
                
                    Shakiel Mahjouri                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
"They want to talk about stats?" Hokit continued. "Let's talk about the Unified Rules. Judges score on effective striking and impact, not patting someone with light, non damaging touches. Ciryl sprinted away from me for 3 straight rounds while I relentlessly stalked him down and landed the heavier shots. Volume that doesn't hurt nobody isn't winning a fight. Effective Aggressivenes & Ring Generalship belonged to me for the first 3. That's why my coaches thought I was winning going into the 5th and his coach told him he needed a knckout...Lets not forget that."Hokit would go on to point out that, had Gane been deducted a point for the eye poke in the first round, he would have at least earned a draw.Had the referee seen the foul, it's unclear if it would have resulted in an immediate point deduction, but Gane has likely lost the benefit of the doubt when it comes to bending the rules.
Gane has a history of landing eye pokes or illegal blows in his fight, most infamously delivering a poke to both of Tom Aspinall's eyes so bad in their UFC 321 bout that then-champion Aspinall would end up vacating the title, leaving Gane to be elevated to undisputed champion after winning the interim title in Aspinall's absence.Hokit closed by pointing to the lack of fresh challengers for Gane, claiming to be the most interesting rematch available for the champion, who has fought nearly every other contender of note in the division."Look at the division," Hokit wrote. "Almost any fight you make with Ciryl right now is a recycled rematch anyway, whether it's Volkov or Alex. But our war was the best by a mile, and the fans deserve a definitive answer without a finger in my eye that had me seeing triple, 40 seconds into the fight. I earned this. Don't punish me because I am not a bitch. Let's make it right."

title: NBA MVP Rankings: Luka Dončić, Victor Wembanyama in a two-horse race; Stephen Curry's absence speaks volumes - CBS Sports
description: While Shai Gilgeous-Alexander goes for his third straight, he's behind the two other West stars
body:
While Shai Gilgeous-Alexander goes for his third straight, he's behind the two other West stars
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:12 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        We're nearly a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while some people say it's too early to start talking about MVP, we are not among those people. Right now, it's a clear two-horse race: Luka Doncic or Victor Wembanyama? There is a real split on this. Here's where I stand as of Tuesday, Nov. 17. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Luka Dončić, Lakers
The Luka Dončić we're watching right now isn't just the best offensive player in the world. He might be the best in history. Nobody has ever put up anything close to the numbers he is charting at the moment: 39 points per game with seven assists, seven boards, nearly two steals and a positively scorching 66.0 TS%, the latter being a number even the great Stephen Curry has only bested twice in his career. It's early, sure. Dončić isn't likely to keep making 3s at this rate for an entire season, and indeed we've seen some slippage of late (35% over his last four, if you really want to split hairs), but his volume remains, with 4.5 makes a night over that stretch. Dončić remains on track to break Curry's single-season record of 402 3-pointers, and he's done more off-ball shooting than in the past. 
Off catch: 5.9 PPG, up from 3.8 last yearOff screens: 4.2 PPG, up from 2.0 last yearThrow in more transition production and a 53% midrange conversion rate, per Cleaning The Glass, and you're seeing a more diverse scorer, which is to say this isn't just a guy who has started off hot on his step-back 3s (though this is a major factor, too, of course), but a guy piercing defenses from more spots with different shots. If Dončić could actually be any harder to guard than he has been in the past, we're seeing it this season. He's also defending. His 23 steals rank sixth league-wide. Only two players have recovered more defensive loose balls than his eight. Only one has taken more charges than his four. With Dončić as the primary defender, shooters are converting just 36.7% of their shots against a 45.1 expected FG%; that minus-8.6 is the fourth-largest discrepancy among all players who've contested at least 150 shots. Most importantly, the Lakers are 12-2 and tied with the Spurs atop the Western Conference. The Lakers rank as the league's top offense with a rating that balloons to 129.2 points per 100 possessions (which would be an NBA record by a long shot) with Dončić on, and a net rating, as illustrated below, that falls off a cliff when he sits. 
Look, if you have Wembanyama ahead of Dončić in the MVP race a month into the season, nobody is going to argue much with you. The oddsmakers slightly favor Wembanyama (+110 at FanDuel; Dončić is +140), who, as you'll see below, has what would qualify as a potentially unanimous case in most years. But this isn't most years. We got a dude averaging nearly 40 points for a No. 1 seed that nobody expected to be a No. 1 seed. Until one of those things changes, it's hard for me to go against Dončić. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Victor Wembanyama, Spurs
If you think Dončić's plus-35.5 on/off split (it's actually plus-32.2 without filtering for garbage time) is crazy, have a look at Wembanyama's number. 
Yes, you're reading that right. The Spurs, for all their supportive talent, fall by 42.6 points per 100 possessions when Wembanyama leaves the court (plus-29.2 on vs. minus-13.3 off), per Cleaning the Glass. By comparison, the best on/off split that Nikola Jokić has ever recorded is plus-24.8. Curry's best is plus-21.3. LeBron James' is plus-17.8. Go down that list and look at the most impactful on-off splits those guys have ever posted. Wembanyama is in another galaxy. 
And it's important to note that Wembanyama plays on a great team, as all these guys in the graphic have. The fact that there is still so much difference between when Wembanyama is on the court and when he isn't, even in a small sample, is honestly difficult to comprehend. San Antonio's three-guard lineup was supposed to be an experiment, but it's hard to know if Dylan Harper, De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle truly optimize one another or if Wembanyama is enough to make any lineup dominant in spite of traditional issues (like none of those three being a true shooter). Wembanyama is the best defensive player on the planet by an immeasurable amount. Even the stats don't do it justice. He's on pace for north of 350 blocks, a number only four players (Elmore Smith, Mark Eaton, Manute Bol and Hakeem Olajuwon) have eclipsed since blocks became an official stat in 1973, and still it's just as much, if not more, about the shots he deters scorers from even attempting. And why would they? Scorers are making just 33.6% of their shots when Wembanyama is the nearest defender, a 17% drop from their expected 50.4%. That also leads the league among all players who've defended at least 120 shots, and again, it fails to fully capture his defensive dominance. 
The fact that we've gotten this far without talking about Wembanyama's offense, as if it's a mere afterthought for a guy to be averaging 28.6 points and 11.6 rebounds in under 30 minutes a night. Wembanyama is figuring out his hot spots, prioritizing closer-to-the-basket positioning where he is a skyscraper among regular NBA buildings. He's taking two more paint shots per game than he did last season; 43% of his shots are coming from inside four feet, per Cleaning the Glass, up from 38% last season, and his 4.6 dunks per game (up from 2.7 last year) have him on pace to shatter Rudy Gobert's single-season record of 306. If I had to guess, Wembanyama's production is more sustainable than Dončić's. It's hard to imagine Dončić not hitting a rough patch from 3, and he's almost certainly not going to keep scoring 39 points per game. He'll be over 35 points per game when everything is said and done because that's what the Lakers need from him, but there's a burnout factor while Wembanyama is kind of cruising to these numbers, and the defensive impact is as natural as breathing. My gut says Wembanyama will be a clearer MVP favorite by Christmas. Keep an eye on...Assuming Dončić and Wembanyama each get to the mandated 65 games, everyone else is playing for third place at the moment. Which is crazy given the seasons some of the following names are having. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Alperen Sengun, Rockets
One of two players averaging at least 22 points, nine rebounds and seven assists, and the only player to be leading his team in all three categories. The Rockets are 11-4 with the No. 2 offense and Sengun is the center of it all. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jayson Tatum, Celtics
Tatum is averaging his normal 26.5 points per game. The shooting efficiency still hasn't come around, but he is an absolute quarterback on this Celtics team. He draws the doubles, and his 35.1% assist rate, per CTG, is a career high by a mile. The Celtics, for my money, are the best team in the East. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Giannis Antetokounmpo, Heat
Here come the Heat, who have won five straight games, with the last three wins coming over the Cavaliers, Pistons and Rockets. Antetokounmpo is averaging 28.3/12.5/5.2 with 1.3 blocks per game on 60% shooting. He's on fire from the midrange as the Heat are exploiting the soft spots in all the drop coverage they're facing. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Thunder
Gilgeous-Alexander has so much on his plate that it actually creates a clearer path to a third straight MVP if he can somehow lift Oklahoma City above all these injuries. He's trying. The Thunder are 9-5 and he's getting his 30.9 points per game, but his 58.7 true-shooting is down considerably, which makes sense as he has to force tougher shots now with fewer weapons around him. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Stephen Curry, Warriors
Curry's value can perhaps be felt most in his absence. The Warriors have lost three straight since he went out with a torn oblique, the last two by 59 points. The Warriors have outscored opponents by 13.5 points per 100 possessions with Curry on the floor this season and have been outscored by 8.3 points per 100 possessions without him. Along with Yaxel Lendeborg, who's being asked as a rookie to carry an impossibly heavy weight without Curry, Curry remains the only real lifeblood of a team that is still shockingly lifeless without him.
